newsitem.title: UK: Grains Council sees higher wheat crops.
newsitem.headline: Grains Council sees higher wheat crops.

text.p: World wheat production is now expected to rise slightly in 1997 to 585 million tonnes, according to estimates released by the International Grains Council on Thursday.

This is up by five million from a previous estimate by the London-based IGC, an authoritative monitor of supply and demand, made in November. It is also up from an estimated 580 million tonnes in 1996 and only 541 million in 1995 after drought in Russia, Australia and North Africa.
The latest IGC market report sees bigger harvests from the European Union, Russia and Ukraine but falls in Argentina, Canada and Australia.

The grain market is now calmer after a dramatic "spike" in prices about a year ago on supply fears and on news that world stocks were at the lowest in two decades following the droughts in Russia and elsewhere.
Bellwether Chicago wheat futures are trading just below $3.75 per bushel compared with a record $7.50 hit last March.
Thursday's IGC report also cut its forecast of imports by China for 1996/97 to 5.0 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 7.0 million.
Lower imports by the Chinese may also help take the heat out of the grains market and ease pressure on cash-pinched Third World importers.
